title: Animal Champions for Kids! Tallest, Biggest, Loudest
description:
Who is the tallest animal? Who is the biggest? Who has the loudest roar? Pick your answer, then meet three animal champions with Milo the bluebird: the giraffe can peek into an upstairs window, the elephant is as heavy as four cars and cools down with its big ears, and a lion's roar can be heard from up to five miles away.
An interactive animal lesson for kids ages 2-6, with questions to answer, counting, actions to copy, quick checks and a quiz at the end.
facts: The giraffe is the tallest living land animal, 14 to 19 feet tall; a newborn is about 6 feet tall (National Geographic Kids, 'Giraffe').
To drink water, a giraffe must spread its long legs outward and lower its head (National Geographic Kids, 'Giraffe').
The African elephant is the largest living land animal; a male can weigh up to 7.5 tons and a newborn 110 to 264 pounds (San Diego Zoo, 'Elephant').
Elephant ears work like a radiator: flapping them on a hot day cools the blood flowing through them (San Diego Zoo, 'Elephant').

A lion's roar can be heard up to 5 miles (8 km) away (National Geographic); San Diego Zoo's fact sheet gives 5 km (3 miles) under certain conditions. Lions roar to advertise their territory, more often at night and dawn; cubs have spots that fade with age.
Many male lions have a mane; lions live in prides and may rest up to 20-21 hours a day (San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance Library fact sheet, 'Lion').

segments.name: hello
lines: Hello, friends! I am Milo the bluebird.
Today is Animal Champions day!
We will find the tallest, the biggest, and the loudest animals.
Three champions are here. Count them with me. One, two, three!
Are you ready to meet the champions? Let's go!

segments.name: giraffe

lines.t: Who is the tallest animal in the whole world?
Is it the elephant? Or is it the giraffe?

lines: It is the giraffe!
close:giraffe
Here is the fun fact. The giraffe is the tallest animal on land.
Tall, tall, tall! Taller than a horse. Taller than an elephant. Taller than every animal on land.
How tall? Look! A giraffe can peek into an upstairs window.
exhibit
A giraffe is as tall as three grown-ups. One, two, three!
Its long neck helps it reach the leaves at the very top of the tree.
Even a baby giraffe is tall. On the day it is born, it is as tall as a grown-up!
close:giraffe

lines.t: But how does such a tall animal drink water? Hmm.

lines: It spreads its long legs wide, and bends its head way, way down. Slurp!
teach
Say it with me. The giraffe is the tallest!
close:host
Can you stretch up tall like a giraffe? Reach, reach, reach!
Now bend down low to drink, like a giraffe. Down, down, down. Slurp!

lines.t: Quick check! Can a giraffe peek into an upstairs window? Yes, or no?

lines: Yes! Because the giraffe is the tallest of all!
Give yourself a big clap!

short.title: Who Is the Tallest Animal? Giraffe Facts for Kids

segments.name: elephant

lines.t: Who is the biggest animal that walks on land?
Is it the elephant? Or is it the hippo?

lines: It is the elephant!
close:elephant
Here is the fun fact. The elephant is the biggest animal on land.
How heavy is an elephant? As heavy as four cars! Count them with me.
exhibit
One, two, three, four!
exhibit
Big body, big ears, and a big, long trunk!
close:elephant
The trunk works like a hand and like a hose. It can pick up a tiny peanut, or spray a big shower!

lines.t: And why does an elephant have such big ears?

lines: The big ears work like fans! Flap, flap, flap. They help the elephant cool down.
close:elephant
A baby elephant is called a calf.
Even a baby elephant is heavy. It weighs as much as a big grown-up on the day it is born.
Say it with me. The elephant is the biggest!
close:host
Can you stomp like a big elephant? Stomp, stomp, stomp!
Can you flap your arms like big elephant ears? Flap, flap, flap!
So remember. Big ears are for keeping cool!

lines.t: Quick check! An elephant is as heavy as how many cars? Two? Or four?

lines: Four! One, two, three, four!

short.title: An Elephant Is as Heavy as 4 Cars! Count With Milo

segments.name: lion

lines.t: Who has the loudest roar of all the big cats?
Is it the lion? Or is it the tiger?

lines: It is the lion!
close:lion
Here is the fun fact. You can hear a lion's roar from up to five miles away!
exhibit
Five miles is a long, long way. Like the other side of town!
exhibit

lines.t: Why does a lion roar? What do you think?

lines: To tell everyone, this is my home!
Look at that big, fluffy mane! Daddy lions grow a mane around their heads.
close:lion
Lions live in a big family. A lion family is called a pride.
Baby lions are called cubs. Lion cubs are born with spots!
And lions are sleepy cats. They rest for most of the day!

lines.t: So when do lions roar the most? In the day? Or at night?

lines: At night! When the sun goes down, lions get busy, and they roar the most.
Say it with me. The lion has the loudest roar!
close:host
Can you roar like a lion? One, two, three. Roar!

lines.t: Quick check! From how far away can you hear a lion roar? One mile? Or five miles?

lines: Five miles! What a mighty roar!
Give yourself a big cheer!

short.title: How Loud Is a Lion's Roar? Lion Facts for Kids

segments.name: quiz
lines: Wow! We met three animal champions. Now it is quiz time!
Get ready. Think hard!
quiz: Who can peek into an upstairs window?
Who is as heavy as four cars?
Whose roar can you hear from five miles away?

segments.name: goodbye
lines: You learned so many new things today.
Stretch like a giraffe. Stomp like an elephant. And roar like a lion!
Which champion is your favorite?
Thank you for learning with me. Bye-bye, friends! See you next time!
